payload.claim: When a `GhRunner` is given, the resolver picks the parent's absolute newest task row (`rows[-1]`, set at line 235) and, if its state is anything other than `READY_FOR_REVIEW`/`APPROVED`/`MERGE_TRAIN`/`CHANGES_REQUESTED`, unstacks unconditionally at line 236-245 — with no fallback to an older row still genuinely waiting. The design note at lines 233-235 justifies this only for a newest task that is `MERGED` or `REJECTED` ('the pull request the newer one replaced'), but the code applies the same short-circuit to every other state too: `DRAFT`, `QUEUED`, `DIAGNOSING`, `IMPLEMENTING`, `GATING`, `REPAIRING`, `REVIEWING`, `REBUTTING`, `ORPHANED`, `EXHAUSTED`, `MERGE_FAILED`. None of those states mean the newer task's PR replaced the older one's branch; an in-flight or independently-dead newest attempt (no PR opened yet, or one that failed before packaging) says nothing about an older sibling row's still-open, unmerged pull request. `saffron cell` performs no dependency refusal and no scheduling conflict check (confirmed by the 'Out of scope' notes), so nothing prevents a second task existing for the same parent spec while an older task's PR is still legitimately `READY_FOR_REVIEW`/`APPROVED`. In that case the resolver now reports the parent as `unstacked` and cuts the child from the default branch, discarding the parent's real, not-yet-merged work — reversing the 'waiting outranks dead' precedence this same function's own docstring (lines 180-186) and `scheduler._dependency_refusal` (lines 605-612) both document and rely on. None of the three new tests exercise a newest-task state outside `MERGED`/`REJECTED`/`CHANGES_REQUESTED`/open-undecided, so this is untested and the gates cannot see it.
